liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Fire on the Mountain** (3 reviews): Reviewer says Fire is where the show picks up steam, with Estimated into Eyes very hot; Reviewer highlights Scarlet, Fire and Estimated, with Jerry inspired and well supported by the band [13][15][16]
- **Althea** (2 reviews): Reviewer agrees Althea was hot and also praises Friend of the Devil; Reviewer's favorite Althea: laid back, articulate, and lifted by Jerry, Bob and Phil after the last verse [13][21]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Scarlet into Fire pairing possibly the best they have heard [10]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the Estimated, Eyes, then Brent and Drums stretch as great [10]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Reviewer notes Dew was a rarity in 1981 and a welcome treat [13]
- **Jack-A-Roe** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Jack A Roe golden [16]
- **Saint of Circumstance** (1 review): Reviewer says Lost Sailor into Saint was rippin', despite a cut during Sailor [19]
- **Might As Well** (1 other source): Jerrybase lists this as the last known public performance of Might As Well by the Dead [26]
- Reviewer finds C.C. Rider cool, though they consider the first set somewhat weak [10]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-08-12.142955.sbd.healy.streeter.smith.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): soundboard; 26 songs; 181 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd81-08-12.sbd.munder.10548.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 178 min; rated 4.71/5 by 24 [3]. Said about its sound: Starts as a decent audience recording, switching to excellent soundboard during Friend of the Devil; Estimated is audience source; Reviewer finds the soundboard sound poor, contradicting others who call it great; Reviewer suspects the circulating version was damaged, since their own soundboard copy sounds amazing [16][17][19][20][21]
- **gd1981-08-12.153257.sony.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 24 songs; 176 min [5]
- **gd1981-08-12.aud.sirmick.95346.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 24 songs; 171 min [8]. Said about its sound: Early Althea, all of Might As Well and opening of Man Smart sound muffled with more tape hiss; Start of Might As Well is clipped and the first seconds of Althea are missing [8]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's first show traveled to; the old Salt Palace felt like a spaceship inside, and they joined the bus afterward [14]
- Reviewer spent the day driving around the Salt Lake valley and canyons in a borrowed MG Midget before the show [18]
- Reviewer says Dead shows in Salt Lake City always rock and bring out the best [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-08-12.142955.sbd.healy.streeter.smith.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and Matt Smith; source: flac16/48 Source Info:Dan Healy's Master Soundboard Cassettes (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R90/Dolby B)> Frank Streeter's 1st generation 1/4 track Reels @ 3.75 ips… [1]. Also: Matt Smith's audience source supplies part of Alabama Getaway [1]
- **gd81-08-12.sbd.munder.10548.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Reviewer compares the sound to a third-generation cassette of the show, saying this copy is still better; Reviewer's copy came DAT to VHS, has no audience patches, and sounds clean with no hiss [18][19]
- **gd1981-08-12.153257.sony.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Sony Stereo mic > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [5]
- **gd1981-08-12.aud.sirmick.95346.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by SIRMick; source: Unknown Audience Source [8]. Also: Audience recording reassembled into correct running order and pitch corrected against the circulating soundboard; opening Alabama Getaway patched from shnid 10548 [8]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Jerry Garcia: [1981-08-12 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1981-08-12-backstage-pass/) [27]
